item.title: Canadian skier Brendan Mackay wins bronze in halfpipe
item.description: Talk about a dramatic finish. Canada’s Brendan Mackay won bronze in the Olympic men’s freeski halfpipe on the final run of the competition on Friday. item.title: ‘Lighting up the Past’: photographer offers tour through Vancouver’s history of neon signs
item.description: In a city that once rivalled Las Vegas for neon lights, one museum is making sure Vancouver's vibrant history isn't forgotten.

item.title: ‘We encouraged one another’: Fathers of two Tumbler Ridge victims meet
item.description: The father of a 12-year-old boy killed in the Tumbler Ridge shootings says he met with the father of another victim who is fighting for her life in hospital.

item.title: USA routs Slovakia, will face Canada in men’s Olympic hockey gold-medal game

item.title: B.C. property firms say $91M tax bill will jeopardize construction
item.description: B.C. property companies controlled by prominent developer Terry Hui say a tax bill of more than $91 million will jeopardize construction projects.

item.title: ‘Signs of spring’: B.C. premier reacts to U.S. Supreme Court decision on Trump tariffs
item.description: B.C. Premier David Eby seemed more optimistic than he has in a long time after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Trump’s tariffs Friday.

item.title: Tumbler Ridge shooter’s ChatGPT account banned in 2025 for references to violence
item.description: OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, says it banned the account of Tumbler Ridge shooting suspect Jesse Van Rootselaar in 2025 due to references to violence.

item.title: Vancouver fast-tracking early liquor service for Canada Olympic gold medal hockey game
item.description: Some Vancouver bars and restaurants will be pouring pints before sunrise on Sunday morning.

item.title: B.C. paramedics union reaches deal with province, avoiding job action
item.description: The union representing ambulance paramedics and emergency dispatchers in B.C. announced Friday it has reached an agreement in principle with the province.

item.title: ‘Kind of a gut punch’: SFU to lose NCAA-level hockey and lacrosse programs in move away from U.S. system
item.description: Simon Fraser University's move away from U.S. college athletics will bring an end to its NCAA-level lacrosse and travel hockey programs following this season.
